title: The fibre degree of a finite locally free morphism is locally constant
statement:
Let $f:Y\to X$ be a finite locally free morphism of schemes [def-pc-finite-locally-free], i.e. finite, flat and locally of finite presentation. For $x\in X$ with residue field $\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field] let $Y_x=Y\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ be the fibre [def-pc-fibre-product] and
$$\delta_f(x)=\dim_{\kappa(x)}\Gamma(Y_x,\mathcal O_{Y_x}).$$
Then $\delta_f(x)$ is finite for every $x\in X$, and the function $\delta_f:X\to\mathbf Z_{\ge0}$ is locally constant on the underlying topological space of $X$ (every point has an open neighbourhood on which $\delta_f$ is constant). Equivalently, $X=\coprod_{d\ge0}X_d$ with $X_d=\delta_f^{-1}(d)$ open and closed, and $f^{-1}(X_d)\to X_d$ is finite locally free of degree $d$ in the sense of [def-pc-finite-locally-free].

proof.text: Because f is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation, the rank lemma applies to f. It gives a finite-valued rank function r_f on X, locally constant on X, and identifies r_f(x) with the dimension over kappa(x) of Gamma(Y_x, O_{Y_x}). Thus delta_f is finite everywhere and equals r_f.

source.place: Lemma 04MH together with Definition 02KA; the Mathlib rank API packages the stalk-rank/fibre-dimension identification

proof.text: For each d >= 0, let X_d = delta_f^{-1}(d). Since delta_f is locally constant, X_d is open; its complement is the union of the other fibres and is open, so X_d is also closed. The X_d are pairwise disjoint and cover X. For the restriction f_d over X_d, finite, flat, and locally finitely presented are preserved by restricting to an open subscheme, while the rank lemma's base-change statement gives rank d at every point of X_d. Hence f_d is finite locally free of degree d.

proof.text: The equality delta_f = r_f from Step 1 shows that the sets X_d and the degrees of the restricted morphisms in Step 2 are exactly those in the asserted equivalent formulation. Therefore delta_f is locally constant and the stated open-and-closed decomposition holds.

lean.statement: theorem finiteLocallyFree_fiberDimension_isLocallyConstant {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [f.IsFiniteLocallyFree] : let δ : S → ℕ := fun s => (f.fiberToSpecResidueField s).finrankΓ (∀ s : S, Module.Finite (S.residueField s) Γ(f.fiber s, ⊤)) ∧ IsLocallyConstant δ ∧ (∀ d : ℕ, IsClopen (δ ⁻¹' {d})) ∧ (∃ U : ℕ → S.Opens, (∀ d : ℕ, ∀ s : S, s ∈ U d ↔ δ s = d) ∧ (∀ d : ℕ, (f ∣_ U d).IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfDegree d))
